TEST: ruvidi, funozes, vabunan
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

Both nexioms are probably among ruvidi, funozes and vabunan. If the machine lights when any nexiom is present, the first test held none, so both are in the second group. If it needs both nexioms, the second group must contain both. A rule like "exactly one nexiom" is impossible, because a dark first group and a lit second group would then need three nexioms in total.

That leaves three possible pairs: ruvidi + funozes, ruvidi + vabunan, or funozes + vabunan. I'll test ruvidi alone. If it lights, the machine responds to single nexioms and ruvidi is one of them. If it stays dark, either ruvidi isn't a nexiom or the machine needs both. That case can't always be fully resolved with one test left, so I may have to make an informed guess.

TEST: ruvidi
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

Ruvidi alone stayed dark. The results so far fit only two rules:

- **Lights if any nexiom is present:** the first group had none and ruvidi isn't one, so the nexioms must be funozes and vabunan.
- **Lights only when both nexioms are present:** the pair could be ruvidi + funozes, ruvidi + vabunan, or funozes + vabunan.

Other rules don't fit. "Exactly one nexiom" would need three nexioms, and rules where an empty set lights up clash with ruvidi staying dark.

With one test I can't always separate all three pairs. Testing funozes and vabunan together is the best choice. If it lights, the pair is funozes + vabunan under either rule. If it stays dark, it's ruvidi plus one of the other two, and I'll have to guess.

TEST: funozes, vabunan
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have used all your tests. Give your ANSWER now.

The last test rules out the "any nexiom" rule. Under that rule, funozes and vabunan would be the nexioms and the machine would have lit. So the machine must need both nexioms present to light up.

Here is what that means for the results:
- The second test lit, so ruvidi, funozes and vabunan contain both nexioms.
- Funozes and vabunan together stayed dark, so they are not the pair.
- That means ruvidi is a nexiom, together with either funozes or vabunan.

No result separates those last two options, so this is a guess between them.

ANSWER: nexioms = ruvidi, funozes
One last question. If only funozes were on the machine, with nothing else, would it light up? End your message with one line: PROBE: yes or PROBE: no

No, funozes alone would not light the machine.

The four results only fit one rule: the machine lights when both nexioms are on it together.

- **"Any nexiom" is ruled out.** Under that rule, funozes and vabunan would have been the nexioms, so that test should have lit, but it stayed dark.
